bullets.text: Ukraine's President Zelensky stated that the first day of peace talks in the United Arab Emirates, involving delegations from Kyiv, Washington, and Moscow, was constructive.
Malaysia's former Prime Minister Najib Razak has been released from jail to house arrest after being convicted for his involvement in the 1MDB sovereign wealth fund scandal.
Seven people were killed and at least 125 injured in Egypt when two trains collided in al-Ayyat, about 50km from Cairo, prompting President Sisi to order an investigation.
Australia is considering implementing world-first criminal charges for AI companies that fail to prevent harmful conduct by their models, a move that could set a global precedent.
Australian authorities are observing a significant increase in teenage radicalisation, with concerns that some young individuals are nearing the point of carrying out terror attacks.
A national survey revealed that approximately one-in-six Australians are consuming potentially dangerous raw milk products, prompting experts to advise against their consumption.
Treasury yields surged following higher-than-expected inflation data for October, leading to increased speculation that the Federal Reserve may implement another rate hike.
A top Federal Reserve official indicated that policymakers might consider a 50 basis point rate increase if US inflation does not show signs of slowing down.
Peloton's debut junk-bond sale garnered strong investor interest, enabling the fitness company to enlarge the deal and reduce its borrowing costs.
